### Parameter legend

- `a`, `b` — both required.
- `a` / `b` — a `oneOf` group: at least one member must be provided.
- `a`? — the spec marks nothing required, but these are the parameters the endpoint accepts;
  a bare call usually will not work. See Endpoint Details for which combination to send.
- *(none)* — takes no parameters at all.
- A method prefix (**POST**, **DELETE**, **PATCH**) marks a non-GET endpoint; unmarked rows are GET.
- Every endpoint also accepts the `Cache-Control` header (send `no-cache` to bypass the
  response cache — billed at the normal rate) and `Idempotency-Key` (a UUID that makes a
  retry safe; a replay returns the cached payload without double-billing).

## Endpoint Details

_What each endpoint returns and when to reach for it._

### /blog/search — 1cr

Searches naver.com/blog — Korea's dominant long-form blogging platform. Returns ranked posts under `data.items[]` with `title`, `link`, `description` (both HTML-tagged with `<b>` around matched keywords), `bloggername`, `bloggerlink`, and `postdate` (YYYYMMDD).

**Parameters**

- `query`: Free-text search term (UTF-8). Required.
- `display` *(optional)*: Number of items to return per page. Defaults to 10, cap 100; `display=101` returns 400. Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `start` *(optional)*: 1-indexed offset for pagination. Defaults to 1, cap 1000; `start=1001` returns 400. Native upstream cursor param. Send the universal `cursor` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `sort` *(optional)*: Sort order. Accepted values: sim|date. Defaults to `sim` (relevance) when the corpus supports sort. Values outside this corpus's domain are rejected with a 400 before any upstream call.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `start` (offset style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `display`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/blog/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

- `cursor` *(optional)*: Universal pagination cursor. Send `pagination.next_cursor` from the previous response back verbatim — the API maps it to this endpoint's native `start` (offset style). You never construct, decode, or look up a cursor. Omit it for page 1.

### /local/search — 1cr

Searches map.naver.com places — Korean business / point-of-interest catalog. Returns places under `data.items[]` with `title`, `link`, `category`, `description`, `telephone`, `address` (legal-district), `roadAddress` (street), `mapx` / `mapy` (KATEC coordinates). Note: this corpus behaves differently from the others. `display` is capped at 5 and Naver SILENTLY CLAMPS anything higher rather than erroring, and `start` is ignored entirely, so **`local` cannot be paginated**: every page returns the same first 5 places. Verified live 2026-08-03.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Free-text search term (UTF-8). Required.
- `display` *(optional)*: Number of places to return. This corpus caps at 5 and **defaults to 1**, so omitting it returns a single place. Values above 5 are silently clamped by Naver rather than rejected.
- `sort` *(optional)*: Sort order. Accepted values: random|comment (display max 5, start max 1). Defaults to `sim` (relevance) when the corpus supports sort. Values outside this corpus's domain are rejected with a 400 before any upstream call.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/local/search?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /errata — 1cr

Returns Naver's suggested correction for a mistyped Korean query under `data.errata`. Korean typos usually come from hitting the wrong jamo key rather than misspelling a whole word, so a naive edit-distance check does not catch them; this is Naver's own correction used on its search box. An empty `errata` string means the query was already spelled correctly, which is a successful answer, not an error. Latin-script queries also return an empty string.

**Parameters**

- `query`: The possibly-mistyped search term (UTF-8). Required.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/errata?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /adult — 1cr

Returns `data.adult` as `"1"` when Naver classifies the search term as adult-only and `"0"` when it does not. Note both are STRINGS, not booleans. Useful for moderating user-supplied Korean search input before you run it against another endpoint, or for filtering a keyword list you intend to publish.

**Parameters**

- `query`: The search term to classify (UTF-8). Required.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/adult?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /search-trend — 5cr

Returns a relative search-interest time series for a group of Korean keywords from Naver Data Lab, under `data.results[].data[]` as `{period, ratio}` pairs. This is Korea's equivalent of Google Trends, and for the Korean market it is the more meaningful signal because Naver carries the majority of Korean search. Note the keywords form ONE combined series (their volumes are summed), not one series each; to compare terms against each other, call the endpoint once per term. IMPORTANT: `ratio` is a RELATIVE index scaled 0-100 within the window you requested, not an absolute search count, so values are not comparable between two different requests. History starts 2016-01-01; an earlier `start_date` is clamped up to it. A keyword with no measurable volume returns no data points and is not charged.

**Parameters**

- `keywords`: Comma-separated Korean keywords, up to 20, combined into ONE trend series (volumes summed, not compared). Required. To compare terms, issue one call per term.
- `start_date` *(optional)*: Window start, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to 12 months before `end_date`. Clamped up to 2016-01-01, the earliest data Naver holds.
- `end_date` *(optional)*: Window end, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to today.
- `time_unit` *(optional)*: Aggregation bucket: `date`, `week`, or `month` (default `month`).
- `group_name` *(optional)*: Label for the series in the response. Defaults to the first keyword.
- `device` *(optional)*: Restrict to `pc` or `mo` (mobile). Omit for both.
- `gender` *(optional)*: Restrict to `f` or `m`. Omit for both.
- `ages` *(optional)*: Comma-separated age-band codes, `1` to `11` (Naver's eleven bands, finest at the young end: `1` is 0-12, `11` is 60+). NOTE this endpoint uses different codes from `shopping-insight/*`, which takes 10/20/30/40/50/60.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/search-trend?keywords=<keywords>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /shopping-insight/category — 5cr

Returns a relative click-share time series for up to 3 Naver Shopping categories under `data.results[].data[]` as `{period, ratio}` pairs. Set `breakdown` to split one category by `device`, `gender`, or `age` instead of comparing categories. Partly fills the gap left by Naver retiring its Shopping SEARCH corpus on 2026-07-31: this gives demand and click TRENDS for a category, though not individual product listings or prices, which no Naver API offers any more. `ratio` is a relative index within the requested window, not an absolute count. Shopping Insight history starts 2017-08-01 (later than search-trend's 2016-01-01); an earlier `start_date` is clamped up to it. An unknown category id returns no data points and is not charged.

**Parameters**

- `category_code`: Comma-separated Naver Shopping category ids, up to 3 (e.g. `50000000` for 패션의류). Required. When `breakdown` is set, only the first id is used. Naver publishes no category-list API, so see the platform guide for the id table.
- `start_date` *(optional)*: Window start, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to 12 months before `end_date`. Clamped up to 2017-08-01, the earliest Shopping Insight data Naver holds.
- `end_date` *(optional)*: Window end, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to today.
- `time_unit` *(optional)*: Aggregation bucket: `date`, `week`, or `month` (default `month`).
- `device` *(optional)*: Restrict to `pc` or `mo` (mobile). Omit for both.
- `gender` *(optional)*: Restrict to `f` or `m`. Omit for both.
- `ages` *(optional)*: Comma-separated age buckets: `10`, `20`, `30`, `40`, `50`, `60`. NOTE these differ from `search-trend`, which takes 1-11.
- `breakdown` *(optional)*: Split a single category by `device`, `gender`, or `age` instead of comparing several categories.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/shopping-insight/category?category_code=<category_code>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /shopping-insight/keyword — 5cr

Returns a relative click-share time series for up to 5 search keywords WITHIN one Naver Shopping category, under `data.results[].data[]` as `{period, ratio}` pairs. Each keyword gets its OWN comparable series, so this is the endpoint for questions like which product term is gaining share inside 패션의류. Set `breakdown` to split a single keyword by `device`, `gender`, or `age`. `ratio` is a relative index within the requested window, not an absolute count. Shopping Insight history starts 2017-08-01 (later than search-trend's 2016-01-01); an earlier `start_date` is clamped up to it. A keyword with no measurable clicks returns no data points and is not charged.

**Parameters**

- `category_code`: A single Naver Shopping category id to search within (e.g. `50000000`). Required.
- `keyword`: Comma-separated keywords, up to 5, each returned as its own comparable series inside that category. Required. When `breakdown` is set, only the first keyword is used.
- `start_date` *(optional)*: Window start, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to 12 months before `end_date`. Clamped up to 2017-08-01, the earliest Shopping Insight data Naver holds.
- `end_date` *(optional)*: Window end, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Defaults to today.
- `time_unit` *(optional)*: Aggregation bucket: `date`, `week`, or `month` (default `month`).
- `device` *(optional)*: Restrict to `pc` or `mo` (mobile). Omit for both.
- `gender` *(optional)*: Restrict to `f` or `m`. Omit for both.
- `ages` *(optional)*: Comma-separated age buckets: `10`, `20`, `30`, `40`, `50`, `60`. NOTE these differ from `search-trend`, which takes 1-11.
- `breakdown` *(optional)*: Split a single keyword by `device`, `gender`, or `age` instead of comparing several keywords.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/shopping-insight/keyword?category_code=<category_code>&keyword=<keyword>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```

### /brief — 10cr

Fans a single query across Naver News, Blog, Café (community), 지식iN (Q&A), and the Korean web index in parallel, returning each corpus's raw items with the original Korean preserved, plus a volume-by-corpus map and top recent blogs. Add `include=digest` for an English translated synthesis with pull-quotes. The Korea-market brief no western data vendor can produce — all five corpora are native Naver. Paginate each corpus via the opaque `cursor`. Flat 10cr; coverage-based partial refund when a majority of corpora fail. Note `computed.shop_price_range` is retained as a permanent `null` for response-shape stability: Naver retired its Shopping search corpus on 2026-07-31 and offers no replacement.

**Parameters**

- `query`: Search query (Korean or any language).
- `corpora` *(optional)*: CSV subset of news,blog,cafearticle,kin,webkr (default all five). `shop` was retired by Naver on 2026-07-31 and is rejected.
- `display` *(optional)*: Items per corpus (1–100, default 20). Native upstream page-size param. Send the universal `limit` instead — the API maps it to this name for you.
- `start` *(optional)*: 1-indexed offset per corpus (1–1000, default 1). Prefer `cursor` for paging.
- `sort` *(optional)*: sim (relevance, default) or date; kin also point.
- `include` *(optional)*: Set to `digest` for an LLM English digest with translated quotes.
- `cursor` *(optional)*: Opaque pagination token from a prior response's next_cursor.
- `limit` *(optional)*: Universal page size. The API maps it to this endpoint's native `display`.

```bash
curl "https://www.socialcrawl.dev/v1/naver/brief?query=<query>" \
  -H "x-api-key: $SOCIALCRAWL_API_KEY"
```


## Choosing a Naver endpoint

Naver is the Korean internet — Google's share there is small, so for any Korea question this
platform is the primary source, not a supplement.

| Your goal | Use this | Credits |
|-----------|----------|---------|
| One question across the whole Korean internet | `/brief` | 10 |
| Korean blog opinion (the dominant Korean content format) | `/blog/search` | 1 |
| Korean news | `/news/search` | 1 |
| Real people asking real questions (지식iN) | `/kin/search` | 1 |
| Community/forum discussion (카페) | `/cafearticle/search` | 1 |
| General web documents | `/webkr/search` | 1 |
| Reference/definitions | `/encyc/search` | 1 |
| Places and local businesses | `/local/search` | 1 |
| Images | `/image/search` | 1 |
| Is this keyword trending in Korea? | `/search-trend` | 5 |
| What are Koreans clicking on when shopping? | `/shopping-insight/keyword` · `/category` | 5 |

### Start with a 1cr corpus, not the 10cr brief

`/brief` (10cr) fans one query across five Naver corpora and optionally digests the result.
That is convenient, not cheap — it costs the same as ten single-corpus searches. If you know
the question is about consumer opinion, `/blog/search` (1cr) alone usually answers it. Reserve
`/brief` for genuinely open questions where you don't know which corpus holds the answer.

### 지식iN is the voice-of-customer goldmine

`/kin/search` (1cr) is Korea's Q&A site — the closest Korean equivalent to mining Reddit for
what people actually ask before they buy. For audience-question research on a Korean market,
this is the cheapest real signal available.

### Two free-standing helpers

`/errata` (1cr) fixes a mistyped Korean query — useful when the search term came from a
transliteration and returns nothing. `/adult` (1cr) flags whether a term is adult-only, which
matters because adult-flagged terms return empty results rather than an error.

### Cross-platform note

`/v1/search/forums` (10cr) already fuses Naver 지식iN and 카페 with Reddit and Hacker News. If
the question spans both Western and Korean discussion, that one call beats running Naver and
Reddit searches separately. For a *contrast* between the two conversations, `prism/korea-gap`
(40cr) is purpose-built.
